newsitem.title: UK: Greycoat shareholders delay break-up vote.
newsitem.headline: Greycoat shareholders delay break-up vote.

text.p: Shareholders in British property company Greycoat Plc on Thursday opted to postpone for three weeks a vote on a proposal to sell off the company's assets, to await talks between the firm and its rival Moorfield Estates.

Chairman Michael Beckett told an extraordinary general meeting, called by rebel shareholders to consider their plan to split the company up, that a motion to adjourn the vote on the original resolution had been carried and the poll would now take place on Thursday December 5.

The rebel investment fund shareholders are the UK Active Value Fund, IMP UKAV Inc and Chaddesley Investments, and they control 11 percent of the company. They are advised by Brian Myerson's Active Value Advisors.

They had called for a controlled programme of disposals which they said would significantly enhance shareholder value, but, when told that Greycoat was ready to talk to Moorfield on its alternative plan, Myerson asked for three week's grace.

After a vote on postponement, carried by 53 million shares in favour versus about 42 million shares against, Myerson said: "It's an overwhelming vote in favour of shareholder choice. We are supportive of Moorfield in terms of its proposals. We want the board to sit down with them."
Management of Greycoat, which specialises in London property, had said last week that the break-up resolution was not in shareholders best interests and urged them to reject it.
